Sea level may change due to glacial melting, tectonic uplift, subsidence, or thermal expansion.

items: Memorize the 4 core causes of sea-level change: glacial melting, tectonic uplift, subsidence, and thermal expansion.
Note the distinction between land movement causes (tectonic uplift/subsidence) and water volume causes (glacial melting/thermal expansion).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Sea-level changes occur through both climate-driven and tectonic mechanisms.
Glacial melting adds water volume directly into ocean basins.
Tectonic forces alter relative sea level through land uplift and land subsidence.
Thermal expansion causes sea water volume to increase as temperature rises.
